title: Weight and local gravity
criteria: Use mass in kg and force in N.
Calculate weight using the stated local g.
Explain how weight changes while mass stays the same.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Which units correctly distinguish mass and weight?
cpa.guide: Mass measures inertia; weight is gravitational force.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A spring scale reads 42 N. What quantity is it directly reporting?
cpa.guide: Newtons measure force; interpreting a mass would require local g.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A 7 kg object is on a world with g = 4 N/kg. What is its weight?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 5 kg object weighs 65 N at a location. What is local field strength?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A sealed 8 kg instrument moves to a world with half the gravitational field strength. What changes?
options: Its mass halves; its weight stays fixed.
Its weight halves; its mass remains 8 kg.
Both mass and weight must halve.
cpa.guide: Mass is unchanged by location; weight depends on local g.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A student says an astronaut has no mass while orbiting. Which correction is accurate?
options: The astronaut retains mass and can feel weightless while freely falling.
Orbital speed converts all mass to force.
Mass exists only where a scale supports an object.
cpa.guide: Apparent weightlessness does not remove mass or gravitational attraction.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
